study_identification.author_journal_year: Zhang et al., Brain Structure and Function, 2022
study_identification.title: Probing individual-level structural atrophy in frontal glioma patients

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate whether individual frontal glioma patients display unique structural alterations in non-tumoral regions, whether common patterns of structural alterations exist among glioma patients, and whether the individual-level atrophy patterns are correlated with patient-specific tumor characteristics using an individual-level structural abnormality detection method (W-score map).

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: CAT12 (Computational Anatomy Toolbox 12); SPM12; ITK-SNAP v3.8.0 for tumor segmentation

quality_checking_detail.answer: Exclusion criteria included patients with previous cranial surgery, neuropsychiatric comorbidities and any contraindications to MR scanning such as metal implants. Initial cohort of 52 patients and 117 healthy controls was reduced to 45 patients and 51 age-matched healthy controls.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Single-site study (all data acquired with Philips Ingenia 3.0T MRI scanner at Beijing Tiantan Hospital). No multi-site harmonization needed.

response_variable.answer: Gray matter volume; White matter volume (voxel-wise)

predictor_effects.answer: All predictors modeled as fixed effects in GLM

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study uses a general linear model (GLM) to model the relationship between brain volume and age, sex, and TIV. While these are important nuisance variables, the paper does not explicitly discuss handling of other potential nuisance structures such as heteroscedasticity (variance changes with age), potential nonlinear age effects, or spatial autocorrelation. The model appears to assume linear relationships and homoscedastic errors, which may not fully capture all nuisance structure in the data. The choice of |W| > 6 threshold is stated to be for reducing false positives but lacks detailed justification. The study also notes limitations regarding sex and TIV not being well matched between patient and control groups.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: General linear model (GLM) was adopted to discover the relationship between brain volume and variables including age, sex and total intracranial volume (TIV) using the following equation... A threshold of |W|> 6 was selected to generate the SAM for each patient to avoid the possible false positives in the whole brain SAM... the sex and TIV are not well matched between glioma patients and healthy controls.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not report any cross-validation, leave-one-out validation, or other internal validation approaches using the healthy control dataset. The normative model is built on all 51 healthy controls and then applied to the 45 glioma patients, but no validation metrics (e.g., explained variance, MSLL, correlation, skewness, kurtosis) are reported for the model's performance on held-out healthy controls.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: No explicit text describing validation procedures. The methods section describes model construction and application to patients but does not mention validation steps.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not use an independent healthy control dataset for validation. All healthy controls (n=51) are used to build the normative model, and there is no mention of testing the model on an independent set of healthy controls from the same or different sites.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: No mention of independent validation dataset in the methods or results sections.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study does not validate the normative model on data from a different domain (e.g., different scanner, different site, different population). All data were acquired from a single site using the same scanner (Philips Ingenia 3.0T MRI scanner at Beijing Tiantan Hospital). No external validation is performed.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: All subjects were scanned with a Philips Ingenia 3.0 T MRI scanner at Beijing Tiantan Hospital.

clinical_groups_n.answer: Glioma:45 (Grade II:33; Grade III:10; Grade IV:2)

deviation_metric.answer: W-score (voxel-wise deviation from normative model); threshold |W| > 6 for structural abnormality map (SAM); 8 whole-brain structural abnormality indexes: ipsilateral atrophy ratio, contralateral atrophy ratio, non-cancer atrophy ratio, and relative atrophy ratio (4 for GM and 4 for WM)

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Spearman correlation was used to correlate the abnormality indexes with continuous variables (tumor volume, CCI, MOCA score). Two-sample t-tests were used for categorical variables (TERT mutation, 1p/19q co-deletion, MGMT promoter methylation, histological grade, IDH1). Significance level p < 0.05 with FDR correction for multiple comparisons.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Every glioma patient displayed unique atrophy patterns with overlapping regions mainly in temporal lobe structures (hippocampus, parahippocampus, amygdala, insula, middle/inferior temporal gyrus); abnormality indexes were associated with tumor volume and molecular biomarkers (IDH mutation, 1p/19q co-deletion, TERT mutation).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Every glioma patient displayed unique non-tumoral atrophy patterns. Overlapping GM atrophies were found in temporal lobe structures, especially mesial temporal lobe (MTL: hippocampus, amygdala, parahippocampus), middle temporal gyrus, inferior temporal gyrus, as well as precuneus, lingual gyrus, fusiform, and insula. Right temporal lobe atrophies were more extensive than left side regardless of tumor hemisphere. Overlapping WM atrophies were mainly at bilateral thalamus and pallidum, with contralateral side showing larger atrophy areas. GM/WM relative atrophy ratio negatively correlated with tumor volume (power law distribution; r = -0.671 and -0.684 for GM and WM respectively after excluding grade III/IV patients, both p < 0.0001). WM contralateral atrophy ratio showed significant differences between IDH wild-type and mutation (p < 0.05, FDR corrected). WM relative atrophy ratio differed between 1p/19q co-deletion and non-co-deletion types (p < 0.05, FDR corrected). Both GM/WM relative atrophy ratios showed significant differences between TERT wild-type and mutation (p < 0.05, FDR corrected). No significant relationships were detected between atrophy indexes and MOCA, MGMT, or CCI. MOCA score was negatively correlated with WHO grading (r = -0.356, p = 0.0096).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The optimal threshold for W is not clear; |W| > 6 was chosen to reduce false positives but lacks detailed justification. Sex and TIV are not well matched between glioma patients and healthy controls. Perifocal edema (high signal in T2-FLAIR) was included during tumor segmentation, which may affect WM-related structural abnormality indexes, especially in high-grade lesions. Relatively small sample size (45 patients, 51 controls) from a single site limits generalizability.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study demonstrates the potential of individual-level structural abnormality mapping for precision medicine in glioma patients. The shared atrophy patterns in regions related to cognitive function (MTL, temporal gyrus, precuneus, etc.) may explain why up to 90% of frontal glioma patients show cognitive deficits. The association between structural atrophy patterns and molecular biomarkers (IDH, 1p/19q, TERT) suggests these patterns could assist in presurgical inference about glioma genetics when molecular biomarkers are not available before surgery. Future longitudinal studies are needed to investigate the impact of these atrophy patterns on cognitive impairments.

general_notes.general_notes: This study is focused on glioma patients rather than psychiatric or neurological disorders typically included in normative modeling systematic reviews. However, it demonstrates an application of normative modeling methodology (W-score maps) to individual-level structural abnormality detection. The study extends the W-score method originally developed for Alzheimer's disease to both gray matter and white matter volumes in brain tumor patients. All gliomas were diagnosed according to WHO classification system. Molecular markers analyzed included 1p/19q co-deletion (31 yes, 14 no), IDH1 mutation (39 mutated, 6 wild-type), TERT promoter mutation (30 mutated, 15 wild-type), and MGMT promoter methylation (37 yes, 8 no). MRI acquisition parameters: T1 sequence with TR 6.5 ms, TE 3.0 ms, flip angle 8°, voxel size 1×1×1 mm³, image dimension 256×256×196. Patients also underwent T2-FLAIR imaging. Tumor segmentation was performed using ITK-SNAP software with automatic segmentation followed by manual correction. Normalized images were smoothed with 4-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel. Study was approved by IRB of Beijing Tiantan Hospital and registered at ChiCTR2000031805.
